cases.situation: My brother and sister aren't speaking because of a fight over who hosts Christmas with our dad. Both keep calling me to vent. I want to help without being in the middle. My sister just called again.
cases.reply: That sounds really frustrating, and I'm glad you told me. I love you both, so I'm not going to take sides or pass things along to Dan. I think this needs saying to him directly. Want me to set up a call with the three of us on Sunday? I'll tell him exactly the same thing.
cases.note: Offer to host the conversation, never to carry the message.

cases.situation: My friend Leah is mad at me because I won't take her side against Chloe after their falling out over the bridesmaid thing. She says I'm being fake.
cases.reply: I get that you wanted me in your corner, and I'm sorry that's hard. I'm not taking sides between you and Chloe, and that's not me being fake, it's me caring about you both. I'm still your friend, and I'll still see you at dinner on Friday.
cases.note: Repeat the position calmly and reaffirm the friendship; don't relitigate their fight to prove you're neutral.

cases.situation: Team lead here. Two of my engineers, Omar and Beth, have been sniping at each other in code reviews. I've spoken to each privately; now I'm hosting a joint meeting tomorrow. How do I open it?
cases.reply: Thanks for coming, both of you. I'm not here to decide who was right in past reviews. Let's keep this to how code reviews work from here on: one person talks at a time, and we leave with one thing we both agree to try for the next two weeks. Omar, do you want to start with what a good review looks like to you?
cases.note: Neutral on the history, clear on the rules. Send a written summary of the agreement afterwards.
